pages.title: The Big Book of MCP Server Portals
pages.subtitle: A coloring book about one front door for all your AI tools
pages.caption: Based on real, public Cloudflare docs. One URL, lots of servers, zero fire trucks. Please stay inside the lines. (We will not.)
pages.tip: Color me: everything. Budget: unlimited crayons.
pages.footer: Adapted from Cloudflare docs (CC BY 4.0). Ages 18+ and SREs.
pages.alt: A smiling server tower wearing a crown under a sun

pages.title: Shadows Under The Bed
pages.caption: Every team plugs its AI helper into lots of MCP servers, one at a time, and nobody has the whole list. Some servers hide sneaky instructions in their tool descriptions. Some are left wide open on the network. EEK.
pages.tip: Color me: spooky purple under the bed
pages.grownup: Grown-up version: Cloudflare blog, "Securing the AI Revolution"
pages.alt: Eyes peeking out from under a bed, labeled sneaky tool text, open server, leaky data

pages.caption: Admins put the approved MCP servers into one portal. You point your MCP client at one address that ends in /mcp, and ride the bus to all of them.

pages.title: Knock Once At The Front Door
pages.caption: People log in through Cloudflare Access with the company sign-in they already have. Apps that are not browsers get a polite 401 and do the OAuth dance. Robots talking to robots bring a service token.
pages.tip: Color me: badge shiny, robot proud of its key

pages.title: You Only See Your Toys
pages.caption: Every MCP server has its own Access policies. If you match the Allow policy, that server shows up in your portal. If you don't, it is not there at all. Not even a little.
pages.tip: Color me: ALLOW = green, HIDDEN = very, very quiet

pages.title: Every Server Has Its Own Lock
pages.caption: You log in to the portal once. Then each server that wants its own OAuth sign-in asks you, just for itself. One big key for the portal, plus a little key per server.
pages.tip: Color me: one color per lock, no sharing keys
pages.grownup: Grown-up version: Cloudflare MCP server portals docs, upstream OAuth

pages.title: Turn Off The Scary Tools
pages.caption: By default, every tool from a server shows up. Admins can switch single tools off, or flip to an allowlist and name only the tools people should get.

pages.title: Tools Get Name Tags
pages.caption: Each tool gets its server's name glued on the front, like github_list_issues, so two servers can both have a list tool. That is why server IDs can't have underscores. Admins can also give tools nicknames.
pages.tip: Color me: HELLO in red, like a real sticker

pages.title: All The Tools In Two Tools
pages.caption: Code Mode squishes all the upstream tools into just two: one to search and one to run code. The AI writes a little JavaScript, and it runs in its own sealed-off Dynamic Worker. Admins decide if it is off, optional, on by default, or required.
pages.tip: Color me: the heavy ball the heaviest color

pages.title: Take The Gateway Road
pages.caption: Gateway routing is optional. Turn it on for a server or a whole portal, and the traffic rides through Cloudflare Gateway, which writes HTTP logs and checks for data that should not leave the building.

pages.caption: Some MCP servers live only on your private network. They connect through Cloudflare Tunnel, and Gateway routing has to be on. The OAuth sign-in doors still need to be reachable from the internet.
